fields.headline: STATE DEPARTMENT BUYS PARAVISION TECH
fields.deck: A small-business deal could reach $6.5 million through 2031.

stories.caption:
The U.S. State Department has given facial recognition developer Paravision a contract worth up to $6.5 million. Federal procurement records describe the work as "digital detection/identity assurance."

The department made the award on September 23 and initially obligated $1.3 million. The firm-fixed-price deal could last until September 22, 2031. It was competed under simplified acquisition procedures as a total small-business set-aside, and only one offer came in.

Public award records do not name the Paravision products the department bought. The description overlaps with technology Paravision markets to protect digital identity systems from manipulated and AI-generated faces. The company offers facial recognition, passive liveness detection and deepfake detection. Its deepfake product checks still images and video frames for digital manipulation, and Paravision has expanded it to flag fully synthetic faces made with diffusion models and generative adversarial networks. The contract record does not show which of these capabilities, if any, the award includes.

Separately, the department awarded Paravision a $24,717 purchase order on April 30, described in records as a "purchase card for software license." Records do not say which software was licensed, or whether that buy was an evaluation run ahead of the September contract.

Source: Biometric Update, 17 October 2026

Image: Biometric Update (courtesy)

BACK WITHOUT GPS

frames.mediaQuery: Skydio X10D small unmanned aircraft system

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // X10D / SKYDIO

//Skydio

📍Location not stated in source

Tech: Electronic warfare resilience

Platform: Small unmanned aircraft system

Goal: Keep a small drone flying and returning when GNSS signals are denied or spoofed.

Why: Visual Inertial Odometry and Anchor Points let it navigate and return autonomously in GPS-denied environments.

Traction: Listed by Skydio as on the Blue UAS Cleared list. Operational status not stated in source.

Source: Skydio product page, published date not stated.

Image: DVIDS

The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.

fields.benefit_headline:
A ROCKET MOTOR
SPEEDS EACH SHOT

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // COYOTE BLOCK 2C+RM / RAYTHEON

//Raytheon, an RTX business

📍Arlington, VA

Tech: Counter-drone interceptor

Platform: Coyote interceptor

Goal: Counter evolving drone threats with a faster-launching interceptor that carries a new seeker and warhead.

Why: The upgrade builds on current Coyote variants, which have intercepted hundreds of drones, according to the source.

Ticker: NYSE: RTX

Traction: Three Raytheon-funded developmental tests completed, with the first launches of a Coyote effector fitted with a tactical rocket motor, per RTX.

Raytheon says the Coyote Block 2C+RM program moved from concept to testing in 15 months. The initial test series confirmed early integration with the current counter-drone architecture. Raytheon's Tom Laliberty, president of Land & Air Defense Systems, framed the tests as support for an urgent joint U.S. military mission against changing drone threats.

Source: RTX, 12OCT26

Image: RTX (courtesy)
